descriptionChirho: Piel denominative verb meaning to practice sorcery, engage in witchcraft, or perform magical arts. Used of individual practitioners: a sorceress who must not be allowed to live (Exod 22:18, feminine participle), and one who practices witchcraft listed among abominations forbidden by the Torah (Deut 18:10, masculine participle). Used of a king who practiced sorcery as part of his comprehensive apostasy (2 Chr 33:6, conjugated perfect of Manasseh). Also used substantively of sorcerers as a professional class: Pharaoh summoned the sorcerers of Egypt to counter Moses's signs (Exod 7:11), Nebuchadnezzar called upon sorcerers to interpret his dream (Dan 2:2), and Malachi names sorcerers among those against whom the LORD will testify at the coming judgment (Mal 3:5). All occurrences reflect the same basic meaning of practicing magical arts, whether as participle, perfect, or substantival participle.
